```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)

# The data file, groups and main outcome are set in settings.R.
# The files sit next to this report, so there is no path to set.
source("settings.R")
hh <- read_dta(data_file)
```

## What we expect from the data

```{r expectations}
# Every variable this report uses, checked against the data dictionary
# (139-household-analysis-dictionary.md) before we use it. If the data don't
# match, the report stops here instead of showing wrong numbers.

# Unit of observation: one consenting household submission. ID: key.
stopifnot(nrow(hh) == 1254,
          !anyNA(hh$key), !anyDuplicated(hh$key))

# village_id (A3): village code, 12 villages, never missing
stopifnot(!anyNA(hh$village_id),
          n_distinct(hh$village_id) == 12)

# hh_watersource (C7): a category, not a number. 1 Piped, 2 Protected well,
# 3 River or stream, 4 Trucked, -666 Other. 8 missing (don't know/declined).
stopifnot(all(hh$hh_watersource %in% c(1:4, -666, NA)),
          sum(is.na(hh$hh_watersource)) == 8)

# treat_chlorine (E1): days in the past 7, so 0-7. 9 missing (don't
# know/declined). 3 answers above 7 (up to 12) are impossible, but they are
# kept in the data for the HFC session.
stopifnot(sum(is.na(hh$treat_chlorine)) == 9,
          min(hh$treat_chlorine, na.rm = TRUE) == 0,
          max(hh$treat_chlorine, na.rm = TRUE) == 12,
          sum(hh$treat_chlorine > 7, na.rm = TRUE) == 3)

# treat_chlorine_any: 1 if E1 > 0, 0 if E1 = 0. Missing exactly when E1 is.
stopifnot(all(hh$treat_chlorine_any %in% c(0, 1, NA)),
          all(is.na(hh$treat_chlorine_any) == is.na(hh$treat_chlorine)))

# treat_boil (E2): days in the past 7, so 0-7. 8 missing (don't
# know/declined). 2 answers above 7 (up to 10) are kept, as for E1.
stopifnot(sum(is.na(hh$treat_boil)) == 8,
          min(hh$treat_boil, na.rm = TRUE) == 0,
          max(hh$treat_boil, na.rm = TRUE) == 10,
          sum(hh$treat_boil > 7, na.rm = TRUE) == 2)
```

## Summary

This report covers **`r format(nrow(hh), big.mark = ",")` households**. Of the `r format(sum(!is.na(hh[[main_outcome]])), big.mark = ",")` that answered E1, **`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * mean(hh[[main_outcome]], na.rm = TRUE))`%** added chlorine to their drinking water on at least one day in the past week.

## Descriptives by water source

```{r descriptives, eval = FALSE}
# STEP 4: replace each ___ with a variable name, then set eval = TRUE above.
# The water source is a category: as_factor() shows its labels, not its codes.
hh %>%
  group_by(water_source = as_factor(.data[[group_var]])) %>%
  summarise(households      = n(),
            answered_E1     = sum(!is.na(.data[[main_outcome]])),
            chlorinated_pct = 100 * mean(.data[[main_outcome]], na.rm = TRUE),
            chlorine_days   = mean(___, na.rm = TRUE),    # days chlorine added
            boil_days       = mean(___, na.rm = TRUE)) %>% # days water boiled
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)
```

## Main outcome by village

```{r figure, eval = FALSE, fig.height = 3.5}
# STEP 4: replace the ___ with a variable name, then set eval = TRUE above.
# The village is a code, not a number: factor() makes one bar per village.
hh %>%
  group_by(village = factor(___)) %>%                     # village
  summarise(chlorinated_pct = 100 * mean(.data[[main_outcome]], na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(village, chlorinated_pct)) +
  geom_col() +
  labs(x = "Village", y = "Chlorinated, past 7 days (%)")
```
